messages.author: 4b06c0bae2d1991d
messages.subject: ZIM-IRT
parts:
So I read this article, which you're the final author on: http://dx.doi.org/10.1177/0962280220907625 

I notice that the DC-IRT was fit in mirt but the zero-inflated model (ZIM) GRM was fit in MPlus. I know mirt can fit a dichotomous ZIM, but is it possible to fit a ZIM-GRM with mirt? 

I've tried modifying the example to allow graded items, but the results don't make sense. I tried this:

ZIMmodel <- "F = 1-8
          START [MIXTURE_1] = (GROUP, MEAN_1, -100), (GROUP, COV_11, .00001),
             (1-8, a1, 1.0), (1-8, d1, 0),(1-8,d2,-.001),(1-8,d3,-0.002),(1-8,d4,-0.003)
          FIXED [MIXTURE_1] = (GROUP, MEAN_1), (GROUP, COV_11),
             (1-8, a1), (1-8, d1),(1-8, d2),(1-8, d3),(1-8, d4)"

I'm just getting odd results. About 70% of respondents have all 0's (to the items to which they responded; fair amount of missing data) but the zero class proportion is 0.001. Unfortunately I can't share the data (at least not without permission from some of my co-researchers), but I want to make sure I'm not making an obvious mistake before trying to get that permission.

Thanks,
Aaron

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: ZIM-IRT
parts:
It's not possible to do this in mirt just yet (though thanks for trying :-) ). There's an identification constraint imposed on the second 'normal population' mixture that isn't imposed in mirt but can be added to Mplus. This is actually why we opted to use Mplus in the study over mirt as at the time there wasn't much point in using new software to compare old software results. At some point this could be added down the road, and then compared to Mplus to determine whether the alternative software implementation is viable. 

Phil
